projects.title: CashDB: A Leaderless Quorum Key-Value Store with a Bank-Test Harness
projects.pitch: Build a small replicated KV store that uses ABD majority quorums for linearizable reads and writes, then add read-repair and replica catch-up. Model it on the CashDB example from the talk and verify it with a Bank Test: concurrent transfers under injected partitions must preserve total balance. You end up with a working leaderless database and a clear view of where it fails under contention.
stack: Rust 1.100 (DropGuard for rollback on failed quorum rounds)
toxiproxy or a custom fault-injection layer
you_will_learn: Quorum intersection and why ABD needs a write-back phase on reads
Linearizability vs. eventual consistency, observed directly
Replica catch-up, read-repair, and anti-entropy
Contention latency in leaderless protocols compared with leader-based multi-Paxos
Workload-based verification (Bank Test) and checking histories for linearizability
milestones: Single-node KV with versioned (timestamp, node-id) registers
3–5 replica cluster with ABD two-phase write and read-with-write-back
Fault injection: partitions, delayed messages, node crashes
Bank Test workload plus a linearizability checker (port a minimal Knossos/Porcupine)
Read-repair and background anti-entropy with Merkle-tree diffing
Write-up benchmarking p99 latency under contention vs. a leader-based baseline

projects.title: Federated Local LLM Gateway with Priority Scheduling and Prefix Caching
projects.pitch: Write a gateway that places one OpenAI-compatible endpoint in front of several heterogeneous machines running llama.cpp or Ollama. Interactive chat requests should preempt background agent jobs. Load is weighted by measured tokens per second, prompts that share a prefix are routed to the same node for KV-cache reuse, and nodes can join or fail without dropping streams.
stack: SQLite WAL for a durable token log
you_will_learn: Priority queues and preemption for mixed interactive and batch workloads
Speed-weighted load balancing and health checking
Cache-affinity routing (consistent hashing on prompt-prefix hashes)
Backpressure and admission control when every node is saturated
Durable logging of a stream so it can resume after failover
Measuring time-to-first-token and tail latency
milestones: Reverse proxy that streams completions from a single backend
Node registry with heartbeats and per-node tokens/sec measurement
Two-class priority scheduler with bounded queues and 429 backpressure
Prefix-hash affinity routing, with cache-hit rate measured
Token log in SQLite so a stream can resume on another node after a crash
Dashboard comparing TTFT against plain Ollama under mixed load

projects.title: Mini LSM Engine with Amplification Instrumentation
projects.pitch: Build a small LSM-tree storage engine (memtable, WAL, SSTables, compaction, Bloom filters). Instrument it so every logical get or put reports the physical bytes it read and wrote. Then compare leveled and tiered compaction and show the read, write, and space amplification trade-offs with your own graphs.
stack: Rust 1.100 (custom Allocator trait for an arena memtable)
you_will_learn: Write-ahead logging and crash recovery
How SSTables are structured: sparse indexes and block layout
Bloom filters and how their false-positive rate affects read amplification
Leveled vs. tiered compaction and their amplification trade-offs
How a block cache interacts with compaction
milestones: Arena-allocated skiplist memtable plus WAL with recovery tests
Flush to immutable SSTables with a sparse index
Per-SSTable Bloom filters, with their effect measured on missing-key reads
Leveled compaction, then tiered as a switchable strategy
Counters for logical vs. physical bytes, plotted for YCSB-like workloads
LRU block cache with hit-rate metrics

projects.title: Snapshot-Restored MicroVM Sandbox for Agent Tool Calls
projects.pitch: Build a sandbox runner in which each agent conversation gets its own Firecracker or Cloud Hypervisor microVM, restored from a snapshot in milliseconds. Credentials never enter the VM: a host-side proxy enforces per-conversation permissions and injects auth headers. Add plan approval and named undo, the propose/approve/execute flow the trending Blender MCP copilots popularized, so every tool call can be reviewed and rolled back.
you_will_learn: VM snapshot/restore and copy-on-write memory for fast cold starts
Isolation boundaries and keeping secrets out of untrusted environments
Policy enforcement at an egress proxy
Treating each tool call as an auditable transaction with rollback
Pool management: pre-warming, eviction, and resource limits
milestones: Boot a minimal microVM and capture a snapshot after init
Restore-per-conversation with p50/p99 startup timing
Host egress proxy with allowlists and credential injection
MCP server exposing tools whose calls go through a propose → approve → execute queue
Filesystem checkpoint before each step, plus named undo
Warm pool with backpressure when capacity is exhausted

projects.title: Fan-Out Load Lab: Reproducing the Emoji-Reaction Thundering Herd
projects.pitch: Build a WebSocket chat backend and a load generator that can hold 100k+ connections from one machine, then reproduce Slack's thundering herd: a single reaction in a huge channel fanning out to every member. Fix it step by step with coalescing, batching, and per-connection backpressure, measuring each change with acceptance tests written as data tables.
stack: Redis Streams or NATS for pub/sub
you_will_learn: Fan-out on write vs. fan-out on read
Event coalescing and debouncing to tame thundering herds
Per-connection send buffers, slow-consumer detection, and backpressure
OS limits for large connection counts (file descriptors, ephemeral ports, epoll)
Tests-as-data: declarative latency/delivery acceptance specs that an AI agent cannot quietly weaken
milestones: Naive broadcast server with channels and reactions
Load generator ramping to 100k connections with latency histograms
Reproduce herd collapse: one channel with 50k members and a reaction storm
Add server-side coalescing (reaction count deltas every 250ms)
Bounded per-client queues with drop/disconnect policies for slow consumers
Table-driven acceptance tests asserting p99 delivery and zero-loss invariants
